name: Alignment of the Misaligned
beta: Pull the same overhang as the neighbouring route Second Thoughts, then keep going directly upward past one bolt to a pine used as the anchor.
overview: A short face variation that pulls over the Second Thoughts bulge and goes directly up past a single bolt.

name: Anaconda
beta: The first pitch holds the crux, jamming the obvious overhanging crack up to a belay equipped with bolts. You can lower off there or carry on to an offset crack on pitch 2, and then swing over a roof on pitch 3 before easy ground to the summit.
overview: One of the hardest crack climbs in Colorado, a steeply overhanging seam above a ledge system on the West Owl. It was an aid horror for decades before its first free ascent, and remains a famous test piece of Lumpy Ridge.

current.area_walk_in: Take the trail toward Gem Lake, and just beyond the first aspens turn onto a spur that doubles back leftward and ascends the hillside under the Lower Owls' western face. The spur keeps rising up a gully until it meets the Roosting Ramp's far western tip.

name: Anaconda
beta: Unbroken crack climbing on the lean-over northern corner of this tower. Link past the first possible hanging stance; a rack of nuts handles it, and the way down is a rappel east followed by the east ledges.
overview: A standout climb on the Tower of Babel's leaning northern corner, near the far end of its formation.

name: Arapaho Peaks Traverse
beta: Trail to South Arapaho: follow the Arapaho Pass trail to the Fourth of July Mine ruins, then switch back northeast on the signed Arapaho Glacier trail. It climbs steadily above treeline to the saddle southeast of South Arapaho, where the trail ends and a rocky, loose Class 2 scramble past a false summit leads to the top. The traverse: from South Arapaho's summit, follow the connecting ridge north, about three quarters of a mile one way. Almost all of it is Class 3, with roughly 300 ft of downclimbing and 400 ft of climbing each way, including a somewhat exposed Class 3 downclimb of about 50 ft early on. Stay near the crest and escape to the west side at difficulties; the east side drops to the glacier. Occasional painted marks and cairns show the line but are sparse. The crux: about three quarters of the way to North Arapaho, two short steps of roughly 8-10 ft each go at Class 4 on good holds; some parties find a line that stays Class 3. Final slopes: easier ground, sometimes with a lingering snow patch, leads to North Arapaho's broad summit. Allow at least an hour each way on the ridge.
overview: A classic ridge scramble linking the two Arapaho Peaks, finishing on North Arapaho, the highest summit in the Indian Peaks. A good trail leads to South Arapaho, then a sustained, exposed Class 3 ridge with a brief Class 4 crux leads north above the Arapaho Glacier. Most parties return the same way, back over South Arapaho.

current.approach: From the Fourth of July Trailhead, take the Arapaho Pass trail past the Diamond Lake junction (about 1.1 mi) to the Fourth of July Mine ruins (about 2 mi). Turn sharply back to the northeast onto the signed Arapaho Glacier trail and follow it above treeline to the saddle on South Arapaho's southeast shoulder (about 12,700 ft), then scramble to South Arapaho's summit (about 4 mi from the trailhead).
current.descent: Reverse the traverse south to South Arapaho, then descend the Arapaho Glacier trail and Arapaho Pass trail back to the trailhead. Descending the east side of the ridge toward the glacier is not an option: that basin is closed to all entry.

name: Arc de Triumph
beta: Start exactly as for the neighbouring route Jester: four bolts take you across the roof, then onto the face above.
overview: A short bolted line on the Fourth Flatiron that starts like Jester, then follows four bolts through a roof and onto the wall above.

name: Arcturus
beta: The start ledge is reached by a delicate downclimb. Face climb to gain the thin cracks, stemming the corner, then jam the strenuous finger-width crack as it trends rightward, finishing on gravelly easier rock. Bring thin gear for the crack.
overview: A one-pitch route on the southern flank of Scorpio Dome, climbing a shallow corner that leans right under a triangular roof. It is strenuous and a little awkward to start, but finishes on easier, loose ground.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: from a ledge lower than and to the right of the Scorpio Crack terrace, reached by a tricky downclimb

name: Arkansas Patriot (aka Wonderin' Where the Lions Are)
beta: A steep slab with a trio of fixed bolts plus a dike to use, ending at chained anchors; carry a few nuts as extra insurance.
overview: A short, steep slab at the west end of the crag, mixing three bolts with a few nuts along a dike up to chains; a common first lead of the day.

overview: Four bolts up a very steep wall on Cottontail Crag's south side, branching off the Destroyer start.

name: Do the Right Thing
beta: Start in the gap separating the freestanding block from the cliff. Reaching the first of four bolts is the crux, so use a stick-clip if possible; above, pockets and edges make for pleasant face climbing.
overview: A solid face climb that starts in the narrow gap behind a boulder. The hard part is getting to bolt one; pockets and edges ease things afterward.

name: Back to the Future
beta: Follows a dark streak of water stain on the wall's southern side. Powerful pocket pulls over the opening 30 feet lead to a rest, then strenuous moves up a faint crack get you over a small overhang to the anchors.
overview: A mega-classic and among the busiest routes at the area. It follows the dark seep stain at the wall's southern end: powerful pocket pulls up the first 30 ft lead to a rest, then strenuous moves via an incipient crack over a little overhang.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the dirt road up from the lot past 2150 Wall and the Piggy Bank, then continue along the base of the cliff to this wall. Expect a short walk of several minutes.

name: Bad Boys Bolt
beta: Begin where the trees cast shade, climb leftward past two bolts, and merge with the neighbouring route Between Nothingness and Eternity. The climbing above is easier.

name: Banana Peels
beta: Squeeze up the deep chimney separating Bonzo from Kor's Flake, which marks the western edge of the buttress; this chimney is also the rappel-in point for a neighbouring route.
overview: A four-pitch chimney climb that splits Turnkorner Buttress from Guillotine Wall, staying in one parallel-sided slot up to the saddle behind the buttress.

current.area_walk_in: Walk the Black Canyon trail westward, passing under the entire west side of Lumpy Ridge, for two stiff miles. A little cairn flags the spur path, which winds up the steep forested hillside under the buttress and finishes close to an enormous flake propped against Turnkorner Buttress.

name: Bandito
beta: The opening moves are the crux and are difficult to protect, so pack wires, TCUs and some mid-size cams. Descend by the rappel route used for the neighbouring route Don Juan.
overview: A single-pitch finger crack on Sunday Wall that leads to a large terrace. The opening moves are the hardest and give little chance to place gear.

current.location: just east of Don Juan at the base

name: How Bizarre
beta: Follow a corner toward the wall's left-hand end, then finish with a hand traverse rightward at the top, clipping five bolts along the way.
overview: Climbs a corner on the wall's left portion, then ends with a hand traverse heading right.

name: Batman's Girdle
beta: This traversing line starts up Carpenter's Corner, then crosses the whole rock to join the last pitch of Hand Jive over six pitches, with a downclimb near the foot of a neighbouring dihedral along the way.
overview: A long girdle of Batman Rock: it starts up Carpenter's Corner and works across the cliff, including a downclimb, to finish on the last pitch of Hand Jive.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the upper path, veer left where it meets the trail toward Little Twin Owls, and bear right at the cairn marking a new split to reach the Coors Roof zone; the other branch heads for Checkerboard Rock. name: Beer Barrel Buttress
beta: Scramble up to a pedestal, then follow the spotless buttress overhead, clipping five bolts to reach cold-shut anchors. Do not fumble the opening clips, or a fall would land you on the pedestal.
overview: A clean five-bolt buttress climbed from a pedestal; clip carefully low down.

name: Beer for Breakfast
beta: A groove with no protection leads to a slim, tapering overhang; stride over it to finish at anchors. The first pitch begins right of the neighbouring route Jazzman and follows a corner onto the adjacent slab.
overview: A groove with no protection leads to a slim, pointed roof that is stepped over before the anchors. The first pitch of the alternative line uses a corner facing right.

name: Between Nothingness and Eternity
beta: Trend rightward on very thin edges and precarious smears, clipping five bolts, up to an easy but runout slab. Belay off boulders sitting on the ramp higher up.
overview: A bolted face climb on the lower wall of the South Slabs, built from tiny edges and delicate smears. The slab above the bolts is easy but runout.

A groove then leads to a boulder-strewn ledge; climb the corner above, mantel up onto a finger-width crack where the corner swings left, then follow a much tighter crack to two old bolts (back them up).
overview: A former aid line, now free: a left-facing corner high on the west side leads to a finger crack and a desperate thin crack ending at an old bolt belay.

name: Birdland
beta: Edge straight up from the trees to a bolt, then work left into the water groove covered in crystals, climb it, and drift leftward onto a seam that accepts big nuts and small cams. Pay out the rope all the way to the ramp where you belay.
overview: A fine but runout line on the slab's right-hand portion, mixing crystal-studded face with a water groove and a final crack. Protection is sparse, so it suits the confident.

name: Wire Man
beta: Follow the seam-crack as it angles right. The crux comes right off the ground, with thin laybacks and pinching undercling holds. Bring small wired nuts and RPs low and cams higher; the descent is a rappel from a two-bolt anchor on top of the corner.
overview: A seam crack that trends rightward up the rock. The hard part is low down, where thin laybacking and pinching undercling holds are needed.

name: Bonzo

overview: A one-pitch hanging corner on Turnkorner Buttress: a spicy 5.9 entry from the left leads to a strenuous jam crack ending at bolts. It also serves as the first pitch of Chain of Command.

beta: Start near Winds of Fortune and pull the roof using a square jug, then run up the face, bear left past a bulge, then end with a fist-width crack. Rappel eastward from a tree afterwards.
overview: Haul over the roof by means of a squared-off jug, work up the face and around a bulge on the left, then finish in a fist-sized crack.

name: Rejoice
beta: Follows roughly the same line as the neighbouring Hot Licks and shares its belays. Wedge up the widening flared crack beside it and veer rightward at a bolt, face climb past three more bolts with a hard move at the final one, then climb a steep dihedral that faces right to finish.
overview: Tracks roughly the course taken by Hot Licks, sharing belays with it. The first lead jams a flared crack, the second face climbs rightward past bolts, and a steep dihedral leaning the other way finishes the route.

name: Borgoff's Blunder
beta: Protection is mostly fixed, but carry long runners to thread through the pockets; large nuts are an optional addition.

name: Bridge of Air
beta: Start atop a boulder beneath the face. Move up and leftward to a small overhang, undercling rightward under it and lean back to a rest beneath a shallow corner. The corner holds the crux, then edge across leftward to a finger-width seam. Descend by double-rope rappel; the upper seam wants TCUs plus small cams.
overview: A brilliant classic on the left portion of a handsome face streaked with pale dikes, offering exposed positions, strenuous climbing, excellent gear and fine rock.

name: Buck Fever
beta: Crawl through the boulder tunnel to the dihedral and jam its crack, then make a tough exit at the crescent roof, leftward, to a bolted stance. Pitch two frictions up a bolted slab. A direct start edges rightward from the boulders past a line of bolts. Bring gear to 3 inches for the crack.
overview: A two-pitch line starting from a tunnel beneath giant boulders at the foot of a right-facing dihedral. A jam crack climbs the corner before the route turns to a bolted slab.

name: Bushes
beta: Pick through the bushes to the dihedral's base, jam up past a bulge and undercling around a big flake, placing small RPs. Belay on a stance with slings, or stretch the rope to a ledge behind a block. Pitch two can merge into a neighbouring crack or follow an easy groove.
overview: Two pitches up a conspicuous dihedral that faces left, low on the Book's right flank. The first pitch holds the main interest.
